issues.description: The Milkable.messageOnMilk method signature is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement UML and the example usage in the template Main expect a parameterless method messageOnMilk(): String (and the textual requirement says it should return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and Goat/Seal implement that signature and include a volume in the returned string). This parameter mismatch will confuse students and prevents code that follows the problem/template (which calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments) from compiling or matching the specified output.
issues.suggestedFix:
Align the Milkable API across all artifacts. Two viable fixes:
1) Preferred: Change the solution to match the problem/template by making Milkable.messageOnMilk() a parameterless method returning String, and update Goat/Seal to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[AnimalType] [name] is milked" (remove volume). Also update any solution code that mentions volume. This keeps the template examples valid.
2) Alternatively: Update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to specify messageOnMilk(double volume) and show usage that passes a volume, and document the expected return format including the volume. Ensure all artifacts consistently use the parameterized signature.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Milkable.messageOnMilk() method with no parameters returning a String (UML and textual description). The solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (different signature) and Seal/Goat implement the double-parameter variant. The template's Main calls m.messageOnMilk() with no argument. This signature mismatch between problem/template and solution creates a clear mapping confusion: students will expect a no-argument method as specified in the exercise, but the reference solution uses a different method contract.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Milkable API: change the solution to match the problem/template by defining Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters returning String, and update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if a volume parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template Main calls to require messageOnMilk(double) and adjust textual requirements accordingly.
